text_fidelity_a: Mellow Shirt Dog Anxiety Calming Wrap, Large, Lime I have an eight-month old toy poodle.She has a very calm, laid-back nature, until she has to ride in a car. Then she shakes, drools excessively, and sometimes vomits, even on very short rides. My vet prescribed an anti-nausea/anti-anxiety medication, and it did help with the vomiting. However, it had to be administered at least two hours before a car ride, and it was not inexpensive. I read a non-fiction book recently called Travels With Casey, about a man who takes a cross-country trip in an RV with his Lab. Casey freaked out during thunderstorms, which is really bad when on the road, so his owner bought him a "Thunder-shirt". First night on the road:thunder and lightning. With his shirt on, Casey didn't even flinch. I was impressed, so I looked up "Thunder-shirts" on Amazon. Actual Thunder-shirt was a bit pricey at $50+ for a six pound puppy, and I'll admit, I was still a bit skeptical about the whole concept. I found the "Mellow Shirt", and the very first reviewer said it calmed her dog to the point of no drooling, no shaking, and no vomiting! This item was also cheaper. After reading many reviews about the Mellow Shirt helping with anxiety about fireworks, separation, and car rides, I decided it was worth a try. When I received it, I let April wear it around the house for a while, because I did not want her to immediately associate it with the car. It fit her perfectly and she actually seemed to enjoy having it on. Ok, after a couple of hours, the test: a car ride of about four miles. My April was a different puppy; for the first time ever she sat up, looked around, even wagged her tail. No drooling, no vomiting, 0 anxiety!!! I have taken her on increasingly longer rides, all with the same result! This simple concept of a hug from a shirt is nothing short of a miracle in my opinion!
text_fidelity_b: Mellow Shirt Dog Anxiety Calming Wrap, Large, Lime

text_fidelity_a:
EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking First, it must be known that the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove, in our case today, with our first go isn't as handy as using the kitchen stove. Said stove which still works at this junction is less than 15 feet as the crow flies from the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove which I set up beside the BBQ grill so as to have a place to set stuff.

We cooked hamburgers, hash brown and pork and beans on the thing awhile ago on a cast iron skillet. Good gracious! I mean a mere piddly handful of twigs cooked the whole meal! It's insane, really. Tell you what...when these things first got popular about 10 years ago I took a look, called it nonsense and never looked back. And then, well, things changed. Our EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove is rightfully the backup for the backup. A real 'just in case' thing. However, were I in it just for fun I could prolly think up a dozen reasons to have one for outdoor fun. But I'm not funning here. I'm very serious. Times are serious.

Not being a metal worker or a brick layer I turned to this device which in all of its simplicity has struck just the right note. It is a little smoky to start, but as it heats up there is very little, just like everyone says. It cooks pretty hot to begin, but by jiggling the sticks we got pretty decent heat control. Smaller sticks for a burst of hot, etc. The next morning I wiped off the outside and spritzed the top and grate with a little spray olive oil as a protectant. I'd estimate that one 5 gal bucket of yard sticks will yield 4-5 complete meals such as I described above.

I'm as pleased as punch, and not a little amazed. What pushed me over was a couple of vids done by EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove's biggest fan in England on YT. In answer to my question he advised that he's had his for over 6 years and uses it regularly. Simple, light weight, and it lasts. If you're circling like I did, go ahead and land on it. You'll be thankin' me. Guaranteed.

Lastly a pro tip. If you are unaccustomed to cooking over wood just be advised to scrub the outside and bottom of your cookware as well as you do the inside. It will get smoky.
text_fidelity_b: EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking

However, I really wish they'd included some directions as it's an experimental, hit-and-miss method of trying to use them. Also, one of the two sticks won't lock. One stick is fine--I could unscrew the pole (twist the pole, not the black part between the segments), pull the length out, and screw until locked on both the bottom and top segments of the stick. The only thing that you might not like about this is the sheer size and the heft. This mess kit is also very easy to clean and the paint doesn't flake off even in high heat. i couldn't believe I got one of this kits for a bargain price but has apart of History in it. Confidence Power Plus Motorized Fitness Treadmill White I should have put this unit together within thirty days but I had other projects that took priority. When I finally opened the box, there were two problems: 1) the directions were terrible; and 2) two screw holes at the base were shorn off. (I think someone had sent the unit back because of this problem, and then, it was sent to me because the exterior box was a bit worn. Let’s put it that way.) The good news is I figured out how to put the unit together myself, without directions, and the shorn screw holes were not vital for the operation of the machine or visible unless you look closely.
Assembly:
There are three screws with a plastic cap. Two are big and one is small. The large ones go behind the monitor and at the bottom of the unit in the front. The small one goes on the left side of the unit in the front. There are two plastic covers that go at the foot of the back of the unit on each side. They screw in with four screws. (Again, I could only use two screws because two of the screw holes were stripped.) That is it for assembly. It was relatively easy to assemble, and the unit works well. I am 5’9” and don’t fall off of it. I like that there are no rails on the side to run into. The price was perfect for my budget, and overall, I am very happy because I hate going to the gym, so, this is a great relatively inexpensive alternative.

text_fidelity_a:
New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red This step counter doesn't count steps very accurately, and the buttons are easy to bump when unclipping the pedometer so that the step information is reset to zero and lost. There have been many times when testing the best way to use this when the steps showed zero when I checked it. In order to not over count steps due to random movement, the steps are not counted until you've done 10 similar steps in a row. Since I do a lot of work in the kitchen and gardening that is under 10 steps, then a pause, then more steps, this means a lot of steps are not being counted. Also, it seems like it is not counting those first 10 steps, either. If I step 50 steps in a row, it only counts like 32 steps. Frankly, an app on my phone works better than this. I had thought a dedicated device would work better, but I guess not. I will note that it seems to count steps better when this is clipped to my shoe rather than to my waistband. I'll update after little bit if I figure out how to make it work better.

The step counter comes with a battery, and you remove the plastic strip preventing connection in order to turn on the pedometer. It is then constantly on, though it does go into a sleep mode when there is no movement. The instructions that come with it are not very clear, but you're supposed to be able to set things like stride length. You hit the mode button to switch between steps, distance, calories burned, time spent walking, speed, the clock, and total steps. There is also a reset button along one edge and a set button along with other edge. You can remove the counter from the clip (mainly to access the battery chamber). My accidental reset problem has been when the buttons are near the top of the clip, where you have to squeeze to release the clip. I still seem to bump the buttons when the ends are switched, but it's not as often.
text_fidelity_b: New Balance Step Counter Pedometer - Belt Clipon Pedometer Fitness Tracker Walking Meter with Removable Base Ideal for Women, Men, Kids to Count Steps, Distance, Calories Burned & Time, Black/Red

text_fidelity_a:
Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring. My husband purchased this for me as a Christmas gift to use in my (finished) basement exercise room. We had been wanting to get something to protect our Berber-style carpet and had looked into options such as puzzle mats, but everything seemed to have drawbacks. My sweet husband found this on his own after careful research. He knew that as a yoga teacher, I would want something non-slip for yoga and/or that I could place a yoga mat on top if needed. However, he also knew that I use my exercise room for strength and cardio workouts as well, and so he wanted a mat that would be safe to walk on with workout shoes.

This Square36 Mat fits all of the above criteria! For yoga, it is as non-slip as my best (Manduka) yoga mat. At first, I was still laying down my regular yoga mat over top the Square36 for practicing yoga, but now, I don't usually bother. Because I have the Extra Large size (8 x 6-Feet), I can comfortably practice in any direction I want, which is wonderful! Now that I'm in my late 40s, I love how the mat provides a bit of extra cushion for cardio workouts. (One note: I am a little careful performing pivoting maneuvers on the mat.) As with yoga, I really appreciate that I can perform cardio routines all over the mat, moving in 360-degrees. Finally, the mat is perfect for strength workouts as well. I can place weights--even heavy kettlebells--on the mat without fear of damaging it.

I did not experience any smell with this mat when it was new, and it flattened out easily once I laid it out. On my flat carpet, it does shift a little. There is no actual movement when I am using the mat, but about once a month, I notice that it has moved back maybe 2-3"; it is easy enough to slide it back into its original position. I've now had the mat for six months, and it still looks as good as when I first got it. The only real care I give it is occasional vacuuming (although I might also wipe it down once and awhile with a damp cloth if something seems to have gotten on it). Overall, I think the Square36 is a very good, versatile mat that I would recommend for the exercise enthusiast.
text_fidelity_b: Square36 Extra Large Exercise Mat 8' x 6' x 7mm Thick. Heavy Duty Gym Mats for Home Workouts Non-Toxic, Non-Slip, For Use With or Without Shoes Exercise Mat - Cardio Workout Mats for Home Gym Flooring.

text_fidelity_a:
LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber Black Badminton Racquet(Air9U Plus) My wife has been wanting us to get into badminton more, but the place (club) we visit sometimes only has lower end rackets, so when I had the chance to grab this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber I took it (for her). She'd played in high school and was looking for something very light and that would be a higher quality. The racket itself is excellent and so far she really likes it. I was able to get another brand for myself (here on Amazon), and in a side-by-side comparison this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber is by far the lighter one. Now when I say 'by far' it is of course relative. If you were to pick up either on it's own you'd have no idea something that "light" could be SO LIGHT, but they both are - separately - then when holding one each - wow this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber shows off its lighter weight! Who knew. It looks great, if that's important to you. It has a great grip and both of us feel extremely comfortable holding it. The head is where the action is, and to our non-professional knowledge, it too is excellent. We've only played a pick up game at home since it arrived, but it was fun, easy for her to use, and gave her everything she was looking for - there was a definite improvement over what we've been using at the club. So far, so good, and she loves the racket.

There is one... "downside" to this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set: the "set" part, in comparison to the set I grabbed for myself, is lesser-than. This LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set only has the racket and the bag, but even the bag is less-than; a cloth bag with the logo on it. Nothing more to see here. For the price of the set we thought it would be a big more impressive, but they put their money where the racket is, not the "set." In a side-by-side, mine (for here on amazon at not that much less) came with a really nice bag, replacement grip tape, and a personal towel.

In the end my wife loves this racket, but we're both disappointed by the "set" aspect. If your'e looking to up your game with a lightweight racket, this LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber is a great option and one she'll get a lot of use out of. If you're looking for "more" for your buck, this set underwhelms - don't get me wrong, the bag "works," but the "set' underwhelms.
text_fidelity_b: LANGNING Ultralight Badminton Racket Set, 9U 62gram Tension Full Carbon Fiber Black Badminton Racquet(Air9U Plus)

text_fidelity_a:
Retrospec Luna Exercise Ball SOO PRETTY!! This pink Pearlescent is absolutely gorgeous… And yes I’m talking about a yoga ball!!? I love the set is all inclusive… If you’ve never used a stand for yoga ball… Once you do, you won’t go back- it helps with balance and allows one to be a bit more “daring/flexible“ without angst of the ball slipping. Stand is a “click together” circular structure that once connected stays secure and actually takes effort to undo- it wont come apart otherwise.. which is exactly what you want from a stand.. stable + stationary!

The ridged ball serves a purpose which is something some don’t know about! This has “small ridges” (a few inches apart) that circumference the ball. These help keep a person in place when using (sort of like tire tread although, it’s not grabby!) I see this very beneficial for any who may need a little extra help ie. hindered with Injury, elderly or, just need or lack natural balance..

Although this has a hand pump- be prepared for it to take you a lot of effort/time to inflate- the better part of an hour.. (especially with 75cm size!!) This has a thick outer surface to keep it from puncture/bursting- which is nice to give peace of mind. This has an internal air bladder in case exterior puncture takes place.. it’s made to “break ones fall“ to the ground and let you down slower- so to speak (again, peace of mind!) But, in order to perform accurately- this must be filled taut!! and you’ll be surprised how long this can keep filling to get there. TBH, we ended up using electric pump to make quicker work of the task.. younger with more muscle may not find this as tedious. Just note: this is also compatible with an electric pump and worth getting it out for the job!!

Overall, X1 of better all inclusive sets I’ve seen- it has such an eye on quality and safety Im so impressed. Sold at $22- without hesitation I’d recommend 100%. You won’t find better..!! Hoping this info can help your decision… Stay safe!
text_fidelity_b: Retrospec Luna Exercise Ball

Double walled insulated tumblers are all that my husband and I use for drinks. I always like to have a drink with me and these type tumblers keep them nice and cold all day. My husband uses his for coffee that he takes to work with him every day, and I use mine for my diet Dr. Pepper. He uses his later in day for cold drinks after drinking hot drinks in the morning. The ability to take our drinks with us saves us a lot of money. We used to purchase drinks at drive through windows, or out of drink machines but since discovering what we call "cold cups" we just take our drinks with us. About this mug specifically, I love it. I have several of the name brand expensive tumblers, and this one keeps ice and keeps drinks hot just as well as those costing two or three or times as much. I love that this tumbler holds thirty ounces of drink. That is a lot of drink and since it stays ice cold when using ice with it, I can keep it with me at work for the better part of the day. The lid fits the tumbler perfectly. It has rubber ring to seal the lid tightly so that the cold or heat stays locked into the container. The lid has two holes in the top, one for drinking out of. I purchased stainless steel and hard plastic straws for my tumblers as, I prefer to drink out of a straw, but my husband drinks right out of the cup. However you decide to use it, the top stays smoothly on the tumbler and I haven't had problems with spills and leakage. Of course if you turn it completely upside down it will spill drink out, but using it normally, it doesn't leak at all. The bottom of the tumbler is crafted to fit perfectly in cup holders, making it easy to take on the go. I don't have to worry with rust or corrosion with this tumbler, since it is crafted of strong and durable stainless steel. When we are done using them, I just pop them in the top row of the dishwasher (lid and tumbler) and they come out perfect every time. I can keep ice in my cup overnight, so when I am watching TV on the bedside table, the cup is here with the lid protecting it from spills and keeping drinks ice cold. In the morning, I refill and the ice lasts throughout the day. I plan on purchasing several more for gifts for family members and co-workers and at just under 11.00 delivered to my door, they are affordable too! Since I never know what to buy for the men in the family, I think this would make a perfect gift for them too.

Backyard Champs Corn Hole Outdoor Game USA Stars and Stripes: 2 Regulation MDF Cornhole Boards and 8 Bean Bags, 2 x 3 Foot One game that seems to be quite popular nowadays is cornhole. It’s a simple game and I often find it at local taverns, breweries, etc that have a large outdoor space. It’s also the type of game I find at friend’s houses and so it made sense to get a set of my own, the Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set.

With the American flag design on the two cornhole boards, this set has a patriotic look, which adds to its appeal, since it is certainly better than the plain cornhole boards so common in backyards across America. The boards come complete with bean bags, too, but there is no net to catch the bags, like with some cornhole sets. With this set, the bags will go through the opening and hit the surface beneath, so you need to make sure to place the boards on a reasonably clean surface.

The wood construction of this cornhole set is nice and I like how they attach together with Velcro. There are Velcro strips on the backs of the boards and this makes it easier to carry the boards around. The Velcro keeps them together, so when it comes time to pack up and leave, you almost feel like you’re carrying a single item. They don’t weigh too much either, so it takes little effort to move the boards from place to place.

Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is easy to set up and play straight from the box. The sturdy boards are made to last and the 8 included bean bags weigh 12 oz each, which is heavy enough to make them good for this type of game; less likely to slide past the opening and slide off of the board. The legs fold flat against the backside, so attaching the boards together with the Velcro is easy.

Cornhole is a popular backyard game and since I play it frequently when I go places, I decided it was time to get a game of my own. Backyard Champs Wood Cornhole Set is a very good cornhole game set with a nice design and good durability. It’s a game I recommend for anyone who likes simple, outdoor entertainment for kids and guests.

BOATER'S EDGE Mold & Mildew Stain Remover – 22 OZ (BE1922) This is a pretty decent mildew stain remover. Although it claims to be a “spray it on, wait, and it’s gone” type of application, I found it does require a bit of scrubbing to get the job done.

I first tried it just as a spray-and-wait cleaner and found, while it did lighten things up a bit (I’m using it on plastic chairs and webbing), it was not all that effective. But, when sprayed on, let sit a bit, and then scrubbed with a soft bristle scrub brush, things worked much better.

It’s not too bad in terms of smell. Granted, you won’t be tempted to dab a bit behind each ear but compared with bleach, this is not bad at all. It has sort of a chemically, cleaning fluid smell, but it dissipates pretty quickly. After rinsing I could not smell the cleaner at all on the webbing or plastic.

It does require a good bit of rinsing with clean water to get rid of all traces of the cleaner, especially after use with a scrubber.

It’s not an amazing cleaner, but it gets the job done. A solid 4-stars.
text_fidelity_b: BOATER'S EDGE Mold & Mildew Stain Remover – 22 OZ (BE1922)

Cordless Jump Rope with Counter，LVYOUIF Ropeless Jump Rope Digital Weight Calories Time Setting Skipping Rope Indoor and Outdoor Exercise Adjustable Ropeless Skipping Rope Workout for Men,Women,Kids First off let’s start with the company. They included a card that, as a Amazon Vine reviewer, made me very uncomfortable. They were offering free gifts for reviews but asked that Amazon reviewers not contact them though Amazon for their “account security”. Probably because this violates Amazon’s rules. They also asked that you not post an image of the included card. The email address is from a domain known to have a serious issue with scammers. Please don’t send your email, address, or any account info to them. Needless to say, I had my doubts as soon as I opened it.

I did like it for about a day. Then the blue light died on day two. Still gave it a chance because I can jump rope inside! Counted myself then checked the counter. Perfect match. Tried it again, perfect match. Next two or three times I tried, it didn’t change at all after a good minute or so of jumping. So I tried it off and on for several days. Mixed results. Sometimes it counted perfectly. Sometimes it literally did not count even one jump. Sometimes it did count but was way off. Sometimes it counted Many jumps when I was just holding it in place. It is simply not consistent enough to trust it. If you don’t care about the electronic counter, it is just okay.
text_fidelity_b: Cordless Jump Rope with Counter，LVYOUIF Ropeless Jump Rope Digital Weight Calories Time Setting Skipping Rope Indoor and Outdoor Exercise Adjustable Ropeless Skipping Rope Workout for Men,Women,Kids

LARQ Bottle - Self-Cleaning and Insulated Stainless Steel Water Bottle with Award-winning Design and UV Water Sanitizer, 17oz, Obsidian Black It's important to first say that I returned this large bottle and bought the smaller bottle BUT the functionality is the same. I want to keep water handy but I hate the taste and smell when water in plastic bottles sits around. I was already aware of the value of the UV-C light zapping bacteria, so I was curious as to whether this bottle was worth the price. The short answer is Yes. I like that it's stainless steel rather than plastic; it will keep water cool for several hours (I usually put the bottle in the fridge overnight). And having left the bottle out and unrefrigerated several days after drinking from it, I again found the water to be as fresh as if I had just filled it. So it does work!

Be aware, there are a LOT of copy-cat bottles on the Internet that do NOT do what the Larq bottle does (nor have they been tested to prove they kill the bacteria). Spend your money on THIS one if you can find one -- they've been sold out lately. Good luck!

I did read the item description that said they fit up to 43mm, but I took a chance that they would fit on my 44mm rifle scopes objective lenses.  These are cushioned spring clips.  They are NOT super heavy duty, but they are functional.  They do fit onto a 44mm objective lens.  They could easily be knocked off in the brush, should you have to run thru any.  They do what they are supposed to do, tho.  I shined a flashlight into the unit, and I got no flashback, so I'd say it's good in sunlight.  I also intend to take a small but stout rubber band and put the rubber band over the clamps to help keep the kill flash clamps more snug onto the front of the scope objective lens.  I say again, these will come off if scraped or rubbed very hard against something.  I do believe the best flash killers are the ones that thread directly inside of the objective lenses that have internal threads.  Those options are also a lot more money.  So for the money and function, these flash killers get 5 stars for now.  If they happen to fall off under heavy recoil (I shoot 308 and 30-06), I will change my rating.

TRIPTIPS Portable Foldable Toilet for Car Camping Travel Toilet for Camping I travel and I have severe OCD, so there is not always a bathroom while on the road, and then with OCD there is the fear of germs, panic attacks, hand washing, etc. so using public bathrooms can be traumatic for me, especially gas station restrooms that sometimes look like a horror scene in a movie. Over the years I have searched, in vain, for a small portable travel toilet, but could never find one that would fit in our small car. With a big road trip scheduled this year where part of the way I knew there wasn't going to be any bathrooms, I started to once again look for a portable toilet. I doubted I'd find one as I've been searching for years. But oh.my.goodness! I FINALLY found one!
This little toilet is amazing. We took it on our road trip, both my husband and I made use of it. Each time it was along the route with no toilets for miles. So we just pulled over to the side of the road, set it up on the floorboard of the backseat area of our little Kia Soul. It worked perfectly.
We didn't want to have to keep cleaning the seat after each use, so we simply put a bag down into the hole and folded the top of the bag up and over the seat to act like a seat cover. This also made it super easy to tie up the bag and lift it out for disposal.
You can order disposable toilet bags that come with a powder that gels liquids, or you can just buy the powder itself and do what we did, just used small trash bags from home. This toilet is very small, but I see that as a benefit so that it can actually be used in a small car. I have seen reviews that complain about the size of the opening. Yes, the opening is small, just big enough to make your 'deposits', but honestly, I don't see how someones bum hole or their hooha could be sooooo much larger, wider, or farther apart on their body than the average human that they couldn't fit it over the this toilet hole. This toilet is not meant to be like your toilet seat at home, ergonomic and wide to fit your whole entire backside comfortably while you sit there for 20 minutes flipping through Instagram (please don't do that, it's gross and it can bring on hemorrhoids). This toilet is all about function, getting a job done simply and with as little effort and space needed.
It folds up so nicely we keep it in our car at all times for emergencies. One of the best purchases I have made on Amazon!
text_fidelity_b: TRIPTIPS Portable Foldable Toilet for Car Camping Travel Toilet for Camping

text_fidelity_a:
Srixon Men's Z Cabretta Leather Golf Glove This is a soft, flexible glove that fits comfortably. It is not the most expensive golf glove you could purchase, by any means, and if you prefer not to use leather, it is possible instead to purchase a golf glove made of synthetic leather.

Since there is zero information about this product posted on this Amazon product page, I am including a product description taken from the Srixon website:

"Lycra insert positioned across the knuckles. Cabretta leather for ideal fit and feel. Provides flexibility and added comfort. The Srixon Z-STAR Premium Cabretta gloves use only the highest quality leather to ensure consistent fit and feel. The Cabrex-Esx tanning process uses hybrid resins to maintain the leather's original softness, preventing any hardening of the cabretta leather."

As stated above in the company information, this Srixon golfing glove is made of cabretta leather. The company makes four different gloves, the All-Weather Glove which is their least expensive glove, this particular glove, the Z Star Premium Cabretta Glove which is about 50% more expensive than this glove, and a Rain Glove which is the most expensive glove Srixon makes.

As the name of the product suggests, this glove is made from cabretta leather. Cabretta leather is a particularly soft and pliable leather which is quite strong. It is processed to have a smooth, luxurious finish and, in addition, Srixon coats the cabretta leather it uses with "hybrid resins," in order to maintain the leather's softness without need for additional treatment by the glove's owner. Hybrid resins are a cold-manufactured blend of polyesters, vinyl esters, polyurethanes or epoxies and therefore may give off a strong odor in addition to the normal odors that leather emits due to the chemicals used in the tanning and dyeing processes.

The source of cabretta leather is the hides of "hair sheep," also known as "naked sheep." This type of sheep either does not grow wool or grows a mixture of hair and wool. In each case, the sheep naturally sheds, removing the necessity for shearing, which is a big expense for wool sheep. Hair sheep are raised primarily in the tropics, and increasingly in the USA. They are more hardy and disease resistant than wool sheep and they do well in hot and humid climates. Examples of two popular breeds in the USA are the Dorper and the St. Croix:

The Dorper breed was developed in South Africanis in the 1930's primarily as a meat sheep. It has a mixed, hair-wool coat, and its skin is prized for leatherwork and comprises over 20% of the value of the sheep.

The St. Croix breed is a descendant of the hair sheep of West Africa and was first imported into the USA in 1975. It sheds it's mixed wool-hair coat in the spring.

Srixon Sports USA is primarily known for golf balls, and to a lesser extent for other golf equipment, including its four types of golf gloves. SRI Sports Limited owns both the Cleveland and Srixon golf brands, and in 2008 began global distribution of its products.

Srixon Sports USA is based in Georgia. I could not, however, discover where its products are manufactured. There is no information about this on their website. But given the fact that the company is not shouting to the skies that its products are "made in the USA," I would imagine this product is manufactured in China, India, Thailand or the like. This is unfortunate because there are over 66 leather manufacturing companies right here in the USA. How do I know that? I looked it up, just like I looked up everything I could find out about this company.
text_fidelity_b: Srixon Men's Z Cabretta Leather Golf Glove

Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable) This WAKE stem riser comes with enough spacer-rings to put your existing handlebar riser at the right height and allow the stem cap and long stem bolt to fully engage. There was a little difficulty in keeping the alignment of the now top and bottom sections of this taller riser assembly, but I found getting the top on first and clamping it in position so the gaps in top and bottom line up vertically is easier than putting the tall riser on first and then aligning and tightening the top section with the handlebars to it. It can be done either way, but it took a lot of fussing, tightening and loosening and twisting. Getting that long bolt in to press the stem cap down to hold everything in position is complicated that the fork bearing will keep everything loose without the correct alignment, so you have to keep that as a goal because nothing can have a final position without that important fork bearing being seated. Then, all you need to do is clamp it all together on the bike. This is a 2 part operation: the long bolt and stem cap forces the assembled units together and down, then clamping the top and bottom riser sections together and to the bike for a solid steering connection. I think this better than the older-style threaded stem which depends on that single bolt to hold everything in place.
-Compressing in several dimensions makes it more secure.-
The test ride, once I was satisfied that everything had been aligned and tightened, was different from how the bike had been only an hour ago. My hands, arms and shoulders were at a more natural angle and riding was much easier. This riser extension is only 2.7 inches, but coupled with the top riser and raised handlebars the difference is more than 8 inches overall. A nice, comfortable ride!
There are youtube videos showing this operation in detail. //// It's important to do it properly! ////
text_fidelity_b: Wake Bike Stem Riser Bike Fork Stem Extender Bicycle Handlebar Raiser Head Up Adapter Suitable for Mountain Bike, Road Bike, MTB, BMX, Fixie (Aluminium Alloy, Adjustable)

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software I've been looking at this pedometer for months, reading all the reviews, and agonizing over whether or not to buy it. (A trip to the emergency room last week convinced me that I've GOT to stop putting off walking and get myself in better shape.) That the software tracks both steps and blood pressure is an attractive feature, but I've already got an expensive blood pressure monitor that's not one of the ones that you can download the data from.

Before buying, I first emailed Omron to ask if it's possible to manually enter the blood pressure data, then (because I was having a fit to go on and order it), called them directly to ask. The person I spoke to on the phone said there's no way to manually enter data but that she'd put in a request to add that feature. She was very nice. I went on and ordered two, one for myself and one for my sister, so I could benefit from Omron's instant rebate special that was expiring that day.

THEN...I got a very nice phone call from a guy from Omron, I think his name was John but I'm not sure, who said YES, you CAN manually enter blood pressure data. You can't manually enter pedometer data, but there's a data entry screen for blood pressure and pulse. He took the time to tell me exactly how to get to the screen and said I didn't even have to have the product to download the software and install it. I was thrilled!

Okay, here's what you do: Go to software.omronhealthcare.com. You will see three products that all have the health management software. He said it doesn't matter which one you download because they're all the same, but I discovered that all of them don't have the latest version of the software listed. Check all three and get the one that's the most current because, if you don't, you'll have to uninstall/reinstall the earlier version later.

Once you download the software and unzip it--and THIS IS IMPORTANT--be sure to disable any virus program and deactivate any firewalls BEFORE double-clicking the setup.exe file to install it. As soon as it's finished installing, re-enable the firewalls and virus program immediately.

The program icon should be on your desktop, so you can play around with it while you're waiting for your nifty new pedometer to arrive. In the Weekly Blood Pressure/Pulse graph, to the right, you'll see a yellow View/Enter Data button. It's very small, so keep looking for it if you don't see it right away. It's there. Click on that, enter your data, then save and close. The data you entered will be shaded pink. So I guess, in the future, if you get another blood pressure monitor that you can download the data from, you'll be able to differentiate it from your manually entered data.

I have not attempted yet to export a .CSV file to be sure the manually entered data also exports, but I'll bet it does. Why wouldn't it?

Anyway, I am very pleased and very excited about finally ordering my Omron pedometer. And less than 24 hours after ordering, I got the email that it's shipped. YAY!
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-720ITC Pocket Pedometer with Health Management Software

The Friendly Swede Microfiber Towels for Sports, Gym, Yoga, Travel, Swim, Hiking and Camping, Ultralight and Quick Drying I like using micro fiber towels since they are so lightweight, dry quickly and are pretty absorbent. That makes them great for gym use since they are far easier to tote in a gym bag than a regular cotton towel.

These are some of the nicer micro fiber towels I’ve used. The edges are well hemmed with tight stitching. The fabric is smooth and feels very nice – no rough spots at all. The size (I have the large ones) is ample enough so that one towel works fine for drying after a shower. If you have long hair, however, you’ll probably need to use two towels – one for body drying and one for hair.

The size also makes them useful for a lot of other tasks, such as a temporary cover for car seats when transporting potentially messy items, a beach chair cover, and so on.

As with all micro fiber towels (or cotton towels as well) don’t use fabric softener when washing them since that really cuts down on the towel absorbency. The same with dryer sheets – avoid. I even avoid drying them in a dryer since micro fiber can collect all the dryer lint. It makes for a clean dryer tub, but at the expense of a clotted up micro fiber towel. These dry so quickly that you can just hang them up over a shower rod and in a few hours they’re ready to use.

Good performance, build quality and price. Zero complaints.

But this one appeared to have some advantages the others didn't. There wasn't any instructions on using this cane, but it wasn't too hard to figure out. To adjust the length there are three sections which can be pulled out to make the cane longer. The cane in it's fully collapsed state is 21" long, fully extended its 42". To change the lengths you twist the shafts which loosen or tighten the assembly depending on the direction you twist. You can actually pull out a section completely if you're not careful (it slips back in pretty easily). The tip of the cane is interesting. There is a rubber foot that can be removed which exposes a small diameter metal point, that I assume is for use on icy surfaces (we don't get that too often here in Texas). There is another thing that can be screwed on the end of the cane, some sort of round dome looking thing, I haven't a clue what it's purpose might be.

Over-all I happy with the walking stick, I like that it collapses down like it does for easy storage & carrying. And that it feels like pretty solid support when in use. I'm happy with my purchase.

Jeff & Aimy Women's Lightweight Cotton Bucket Beach Sun Hats Ponytail Hole Wide Brim UV Protection Foldable Travel Fishing Sunhats Gray I am reviewing the Jeff & Aimmy Cotton Vucket Hat in the color " Black#990022", which is gray with a black bow. I was supposed to receive the hat in black ( 00707_black), so that it was may come up under my review. I will include pics of the hat on.

Before you select one, make sure to take a look at the sizing. There are TWO sizes available, Medium OR Large. There is no elastic, nor ability to adjust, so choose wisely.

Medium fits 55-58CM (22.2"-22.8");
Large fits 58-61CM (23.03"- 24.0") ----my head measures 23.75", this fits very well.

Despite that the product description states that the hat is adjustable, it is NOT. The only portion that is "adjustable" is the optional chin strap. On mine, it can be kept clipped on, or taken off. There is a toggle to make it tighter against the face, or allow it to be loose.

The interior has what appears to be an elastic band, but it is not elastic. It's purpose is more like that of a sweat band or to provide some grip, but it doesn't not stretch. This will either fit, or it won't.

I normally like Jeff & Aimmy products, and overall I like this too. I just want to see a cleaned up, more accurate description. (and what are with all the reviews for this product yet are for something not being sold here?)

The material is soft, light. The brim is long but can be folded back some as needed.
The slit for the pony tail is subtle. So it will blend in when not in use. But to use it, is a little awkward as you will have to feed the pony tail through a narrow slit. Not bad though. Doable.

I do appreciate that there are size offerings for larger heads. It is rare- extremely- that I find a womens hat that fits anything above 22.5". MY cranium is 23.75", so I can't wear most stuff. SO unless you have a bigger head like mine, you will most likely be wanting a medium. If your "large" is too big, then you ordered the wrong size as the size large is accurate (23.03"- 24.0"). It will just fit if your head it 24". Might be snug. It fits mine just right at 23.75". Or if your medium is too small.. then again, likely wrong size. selected. Either way, make sure you got what you ordered.

I use sun hats (when I can find them in my size) a lot. I prefer to avoid the sun. I keep it off my face and body, especially during the summer months. Between sun sensitive meds, rosacea, and just wanting added protection from UV rays, a sun hat is a great thing to have. Since I can add this to my list of companies that sell larger sized hats I will possibly be back to purchase more. I like the overall look (even if I did get something different than anticipated).
text_fidelity_b: Jeff & Aimy Women's Lightweight Cotton Bucket Beach Sun Hats Ponytail Hole Wide Brim UV Protection Foldable Travel Fishing Sunhats Gray

Both were for 10 foot rods. The case is actually pretty good considering the price. However, the tube should have some relief cut length wise (4" or so) into the top end to assist in removing the rod. The rod has to be removed straight out the back without any angle but the pouch itself interferes to some degree. A 4" or so notch cut out at the top end would facilitate easy removal. The little storage pouches on the sides might be a nice touch for some but to me they were an unnecessary nuisance. Also, a nice dense closed cell foam fly patch would be nice.

CAUTION: I broke an Orivs 10 foot rod right off the bat putting it in this case. I use this type of case so that I can pull the rod down into two pieces, keep the reel on with the leader and fly so that all I have to do is put it together the next pull over or stream. That is the point of having the reel pouch. When I placed the rod into the case, apparently the tip went into one compartment and the butt into another. When I pushed the r\od all the way in the line came tight against the compartments and snapped the very tip of the rod....My bad, but just a word of caution. I now make certain that both sections of rod go into ONE compartment.
text_fidelity_b: BW Sports Fly Rod and Reel Case for (10 Ft.) 2-Piece Fly Rods - RC 1010

Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack My husband was looking for a day pack. I bought him 6 backpacks to compare. The [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]], the [[ASIN:B00DNTR5CQ Osprey Packs Momentum 22 Daypack (Spring 2016 Model), Carbide Grey]], the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]], the [[ASIN:B00FUWSTI8 Lightweight Rucksack 25L for men women kids - Foldable into Inner pocket (BLACK)]], the [[ASIN:B013K7CJD0 Cycling Hiking Backpack Sunhiker Water Resistant Travel Backpack Lightweight SMALL Daypack M0714 (Dark Green)]], and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. There were pros and cons for each pack. He decided to keep the [[ASIN:B010LAU5CG Hiking Cycling Backpack, Sunhiker Sports Outdoor Backpack Bag Running Camping Backpack Water Resistant Lightweight SMALL Daypack 25L M441 (Black)]]because it met his needs the best. We ordered all packs in gray, green, or black. We returned the other 5 packs. I liked 2 of the lightweight foldable packs - the [[ASIN:B014EMLHDI Outlander Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack, Grey]]and the [[ASIN:B01EH0YGSU Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Backpack Daypack-Lifetime Warranty (New Grey)]]. I decided to order those for myself in Pink and Purple.
All of the packs had a mesh pocket on each side of the pack for water bottles. We tested them all with a Nalgene bottle and a bottle of water. All of the packs could easily hold the bottle of water. Some were a very tight fit for the Nalgene bottles. All packs had a main compartment with one or two pockets in the front of the pack. The main compartments varied from 561 cubic inches to 1386 cubic inches. 3 of the packs were lightweight, foldable, and storable in their own pocket.
Here are my summaries of this pack:
1296 cubic inches
18” x 12” x 6”
7 1/2” mesh pockets
Covers about 6 1/2” of bottles
Straps 2 1/2” wide
This pack has 4 main compartments. In the back is the largest zippered compartment. In the middle is a zippered compartment that extends the entire length of the pack. In the front at the top is a small zippered pocket. In the front on the bottom is another small zippered pocket. This is where the pack is stored when folded.
Pros:
- Very easy to adjust shoulder straps
- Straps are mesh on one side and fabric on the other side. These reinforced straps feel soft and pliable
- Pockets fit a Nalgene bottle
- Handle at top of pack for an additional way of carrying pack
- Large open at top pocket inside the pack against the back
- 4 main compartments rather than the typical 3.
Cons:
- Thinner material than a standard backpack.
- No back padding and did not keep it’s shape. Typical for a foldable pack.
- No small zippered pocket inside the pack.

This was a larger, lightweight, foldable daypack that met my needs, so I ordered it in a different color.
text_fidelity_b: Free Knight 25L Packable Handy Lightweight Travel Hiking Backpack Daypack

text_fidelity_a:
Ryno Tuff 12 Pc Resistance Bands Set - 5 Workout Bands, Cushioned Ankle Straps, Padded Handles, Door Anchor & Waterproof Gym Bag - Home Exercise, Strength Training, Physical Therapy, Yoga Fitness Gear I wanted a new set of resistance bands as my old set was getting pretty old. These Ryno-Tuff Resistance Bands Set are inexpensive and offer a good selection of bands, and - as most sets do - they come with a pair of handles, a pair of ankle straps and a door anchor. The set also includes a bag and a sturdy wall poster of exercises which those new to resistance band training could find very useful.

Let me get one thing out of the way first. The bag is small, and while you could carefully fold up all the bands and stuff the bag to make them fit, I'm not going to use the bag as putting everything into it is a pain. I'll use another bag I have that's more than twice the size so I can get to everything quickly during workouts.

Now the bands themselves. First off, they work, offering a decent amount of resistance per band. I find the material thinner than with brands like Bodylastics, which I used for years and will probably use again. If you pinch one of the thinner Ryno tubes and then one of the Bodylastics tubes, you'll notice the walls of the Ryno tubes are thinner, and don't have the snap-proof cord inside each band. That being said, Bodylastics sets cost more. These Ryno bands will get the job done, although I'm guessing that they won't last as long.

The handles are nicely padded, a plus, although the fabric used for the parts you don't grip is on the thin side, and if I were planning to go heavy with this site, I'd buy stronger handles. The ankle straps are about the same quality you get with some other resistance band sets. If you don't work heavy, they should be fine. I tore the last, very similar set I had working out at about 75 pounds, and bought something studier. I suggest you try these and see how they do for you.

But here's the thing. I have a functional trainer and weights in the house. I prefer resistance bands for certain exercises, and if you want to work out at the beach, in the park or in a hotel room, this is where resistance bands shine. If you travel a lot and prefer to work out in your hotel room, a set of resistance bands takes up little space, doesn't weigh much and are easy to use. Want to catch some rays while you work out or just want to enjoy the outdoors? Resistance bands. And if you don't have room, they're also one of the better, lower cost options.

I'll be honest - these aren't the best quality resistance bands I've used, but they're also far from the worst, and they're inexpensive, which is a plus. They allow you to stack your resistance, the handles are comfy, and the door anchor is pretty good, too. I wouldn't expect these to last as long as more premium bands, but if you don't overstretch them, they should last a while. I'm happy I got them, and I'll be using them for a while. If you're just getting into shape, the poster will be helpful, and if you travel, this set could help you work out anywhere.

mountop Collapsible Water Bottle, Portable Food Grade Silicone Foldable Travel Reusable Leak Proof Water Bottles for Traveling Running Fitness BPA Free, 20oz, Pink [[VIDEOID:9ea66d243a3087e6755a9e76943d7c4a]] *update review below*
First impression is good idea but poor quality. I like the idea of having a portable collapsible flask for theme parks, hiking and traveling on plane (after security checkout).
One design flaw is that the cap is not attached to the flask so you can lose the cap easily since it's so small.
The biggest flaw with this brand compared to the E-Senior brand I tried is that the insides were stuck together like glue. I didn't think silicon could be this sticky (unless there is another chemical making it stick). Now I'm afraid to drink out of it.
It wasn't suction pressure but literally sticking like glue (see video). Could barely even pry insides open. Used a plastic chopstick carefully to help prevent puncturing.
The flask does stand up but the shape is all dented and deformed from being stuck together like the first one.

Also, as with many flasks of this type, it seems like a hit or miss regarding the taste of water when drinking from it. I'm returning this one anyways.
But I was planning to soak insides with lemon and baking soda water overnight and give it a thorough soap wash. But it's off to a bad start. I'll see if a replacement is any better.

*update* Received a replacement. It was still sticky again on the insides and had to get a long chopstick to separate the insides.
I'm returning this one too. I didn't like the idea that the material was sticky inside and I'm gonna be drinking out of it too. Just bad quality.

I tried another brand, E-Senior (probably from same manufacturer as it looks exactly the same), but this brand seems to have better quality for some reason. It even looks like the product pic when standing with a nice rounded rectangular shape. The insides opened up just fine without any stickiness at all. Mabe this company has better quality control.

text_fidelity_a:
Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android The app that accompanies this and the way it works is simple and very neat. I have yet to have a chance to check it vs more expensive industry standards like GC2 or trackman BUT for the most part these devices are accurate unto themselves and it's user error that throws them off.

It does NOT do carry distance (which makes sense if you think about it, it doesn't see what the ball is doing). If you duff a shot fat and hit the deck before the ball, it will register that as your strike.

It has a very cool animation and 3D manipulated graphic and pretty much all the important info in terms of face angle/path/AoA/speed/shaft lean. All very good for the home golf nerd that doesn't have regular access to the big machines.

Where it falls short and loses a star from my perspective is this: The mounting system needs a good bit of work. I left it in my car on a hot day inside the little carrying case it comes in (it latches to a little plastic dowel) and when doing so I THINK it melted the rubber grippers that grab onto the club shaft. So now it doesn't have enough tension to hold onto smooth steel shafts (like on irons). So after a few solid strikes taking divots or some poorly struck shots that rattle the club you will notice that the device is no longer in line with your club face. Who knows how long it's been that way so unless you check every time your data for the day could be total garbage. Another thing, the cover that protects the USB charging port is ALSO the aligning mark. This presents two problems. 1 the darn thing keeps opening and flopping around while I try to swing. 2 This alignment mark which is suppose to assist in the ultimate accuracy of the device is on a component that is NOT securely fashioned onto the device itself.

Bottom line: Quite a fun and when used carefully possibly quite accurate tool to help you make your swing easier to quantify and tangible. Not perfect but maybe there will be a Swingbyte 3 that will address these things :)
text_fidelity_b: Swingbyte 2 Golf Training Device - Golf’s Most Trusted Mobile Swing Analyzer - Includes Mobile App for iPhone and Android

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Discontinued Osprey Salida 8 Women's Bike Hydration Backpack with Hydraulics Reservoir, Teal Glass [[VIDEOID:f899b5904dd638d027a40416fde9e9f1]] This is my first hydration pack and it does not come with any instructions. It took me about one hour to figure everything out--particularly the hydration bladder. However, after using this, I love it. It is extremely well designed, comfortable, and stylish. I also love the color.

PROS
- There's a loop for a light on the bottom of the pack.

- It has a bike helmet clip.

- There's an outer pocket to store clothing.

- The inner pocket has one covered zippered pocket for cell phone, Chapstick, etc. There's also a mesh zippered pocket below that and another folder-like pocket opposite that in addition to the main compartment area for minimal storage.

- Behind the inner pocket is the zippered compartment for the hydration bladder.

- The hydration bladder is 2.5L or 85 ounces. It comes with a handle and the pack has a tiny cinch strap that holds the bladder upright when full so that it does not sink to the bottom of the pack. I did a search on YouTube for "How to fill Osprey Hydration pack," and found Chris SERF's very helpful video. Prior to viewing that video I just could not figure out how to open the main bladder compartment after I got the slide cinch off the bladder.

- The pack has a waist belt and a chest belt with magnetic closure.

- The tubing to the reservoir has a magnetic disk that clips it onto the chest belt area of the pack. There are also various loops through which the tubing can pass.

- The bite valve is removable. Another YouTuber said there is a locking mechanism to lock the bite valve but I could not get it to lock. Sometimes water will leak out of the bite valve but I only had that happen once.

- It has a mesh back to increase air flow which reduces but does not eliminate sweating against the pack.

CONS
- This comes with zero instructions and I could not find a video on the Osprey website on how to fill the hydration bladder. As of this writing, there are also no manuals for the Salida under the customer support section.

- The tubing is about two inches too short for my build. Since the card that came with the pack says the tubing can be cut, I think the tubing should be lengthened as it can always be made shorter but it is impossible to make longer.

- My major complaint is that the water coming out of the bladder tastes awful. It tastes like a new shower curtain smells. I was only able to drink about half a cup as I kept spitting it out. I wrote and tweeted Osprey and they have not yet responded with a solution. However, the YouTuber, Chris MORSF, whose video helped me learn how to open the bladder said that the "Only thing that I can think of is Steriliser tablets like what is used for babies bottles then giving the bladder a very thorough rinse out with water." I have yet to try that.

Overall, I love the way this pack is engineered and how comfortable it is. I used this once so far on a two-hour walk and I did not even know I was wearing this. I had a concern of drying the bladder between use but came up with my own solution of stuffing the bladder mouth with a silicone ramekin (see last photo) and hanging it upside down for several days. It dried in two days and the tubing is almost dry as of day three. If Osprey addressed all three CONS and provided instructions or a link to instructions for a neophyte user like me and how to get rid of that bad taste, I would have rated this five stars. I attached a video that I hope is helpful and some pictures of this Osprey Salida 8 Women's pack.

UPDATE May 14, 2019 - I finally heard from Osprey regarding the two questions I had. I have yet to try either solution.

1 – To get rid of the disgusting plastic flavor of the water, they recommend freezing the reservoir with lemon juice to clean it out. They also have cleaning tablets available that help with the taste.

2- With regard to the bite valve lock being unmovable, they recommend running it under hot water and then twisting it.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Discontinued Osprey Salida 8 Women's Bike Hydration Backpack with Hydraulics Reservoir, Teal Glass

text_fidelity_a: Therm-a-Rest Trail Scout Self-Inflating Foam Camping Mat I had the older model trail scout for 7 years and it served me well. I has around thirty holes in it from cat claws and I want to share the reason I love this particular pad so much. If you use the clear tenacious tape patches on it you don’t need sealant. They stick really well to the surface of this. Just cut to size so it is 1/4 of an inch all around the sides of the hole make sure the area is clean and dry and push the tape down on the surface as hard as you can. It will hold a seal forever on the urethane. Other pads aren’t this simple to patch. Even with thirty holes my old one still holds air after being taped up. Really I didn’t need a new pad at all, but I was curious about the new wing lock valve. The only thing I don’t like about this new pad is the valve. My mouth doesn’t seal around it as well as the old one and the inflation time seems the same. The wing lock is awkward by comparison to the old. I don’t like that I have to manipulate it more and the larger size of the nozzle leaves air to escape around the edges when I blow into it. Maybe it’s just this one? Defective? I don’t know. I should probably contact them and ask if this is a wing lock thing. I am not taking off stars for it. Only thing I would change is to put a layer of Mylar sandwiched between the foam to make it a little bit warmer and still let it be self inflating. If they do that I will never buy another pad. 😂
text_fidelity_b: Therm-a-Rest Trail Scout Self-Inflating Foam Camping Mat

text_fidelity_a:
KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym We have a large array of options for working out - to loose/keep off weight and build and maintain muscle. But among the options we wanted something that we could travel with as well as give us a variety of options at home. Boredom can kill a workout routine.

I specifically chose this set for 1. the variety and choices of weights, 2. The options for use with/without a door, 3. The look of the hand and ankle straps and handles, 4. The look of the ends of the bands - their connector including the carabiner connectors.

1. The variety of weights/resistance allows one to go up to 120 lbs. We are not there, but we have the option. Changing the bands out can give a range of weight options and this was a good one compared to others. It also lets one adjust what they are doing - legs, arms.

2. The options for use with or without a door means one can anchor the bands under one’s foot or in a door. We have a TRX set we use with a door, but this gives us another option - we would be more likely to travel with this set now so if unable to use in a door on a trip we would still have the ability to use our feet. That said, there is something “better” to a TRX version. It feels stronger - but it is slightly heavier, while this set is more complicated with all the items included.

3. The hand and ankle straps appeared average overall, but better than some other sets we were looking at. The handles are a bit “rough,” but not uncomfortable. I have worked them with and without gloves and both are fine. The ankle straps are average in feel, but better than some I’ve experienced. Overall both are just fine.

4. I was mostly concerned that they would have longevity. I looked at how the bands connected to the handles, how they were topped off to keep their own ends secure. Compared to others - via pictures - these appeared to have good, solid endings, and that the make up of how they connect to the handles was a good method. I know the carabiners are the weakest link and I took that into consideration. I think they are pretty solid - based on pictures and how they feel - but I am prepared should they fail - we would be able to change them out for others if needed.

Overall we are happy with this choice. The set is what it appears to be, but compared to many others - and I looked at more than 20 sets - this one had everything we wanted, feels as though it has the longevity and strength we wanted and expect, and will give us another successful workout option.

Happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym

text_fidelity_a:
Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves I have owned a pair of Lee Haney lifting gloves with wrist wrap for 19 years and which I used three times per week for about 12 of those years. I still have those gloves and although they are a bit stiff, you'd never know they were used so much as they hardly look worn. Since the Lee Haney gloves are not padded, I decided to try these gloves both because I expected an increase in comfort and as an enticement to get me back into lifting again.

The gloves I received are a size "Large" and they are heavier than any other lifting gloves I've tried before; the pair weighs in at 6.2 ounces according to my dietary food scale. However, you don't notice the weight when wearing them. Below are the pros and cons I noticed during use:

PROS:

1. The gloves are well padded. In fact, the padding is an excellent feature for when I perform lifts where the weight is in the palm of my hand, such as when doing a bench press or incline press or when the weight is evenly distributed throughout the hand such as when doing squats using a [[ASIN:B0000AVAL2 Advanced Fitness Manta Ray]].

2. I usually take a size medium or large in a woman's glove and this size large fit me comfortably.

3. The extra "leather-like" flap that you secure to the fastened wrist wrap offers extra security so that the wrap won't come undone during a lift and the gloves will remain securely fastened.

CONS:

1. The padding on the pinkie finger was uncomfortable for me when doing dead lifts because the bar was evenly distributed through my hand and the padding on the pinkie finger seemed to get in the way. It almost caused a pressure point of discomfort during each entire lift (ascent and descent).

2. The wrist wrap was awkward to fasten because not only did I have to wrap the strap around my wrist, but then I had to flip over the "leather-like" flap and make sure it fastened to the Velcro on the back of the flap.

3. I was bothered by the white tag inside the right glove during lifting. Perhaps the manufacturer could either leave the tags out or put them on the non-Velcro portion of the wrist wrap.

4. I don't like that the two pieces of fabric used to fasten the glove to the cardboard insert it came with remain sewed to the glove. Basically, the gloves arrive with two tags on each glove that fastens to the cardboard packaging. Those tags remain as part of the glove and to me they are annoying as I see no reason to ever use those tags again.

I do think that if men are considering purchasing these gloves, they might want to consider ordering the next size up. My boyfriend always takes a size "Large" in men's gloves and he had to struggle to get these size Large gloves on his hands.

These gloves are thick and although they feel well-made they don't look well-made on close inspection. Therefore, I'm concerned that the stitching on the padding may come loose. When comparing these gloves to my Lee Haney gloves, I doubt they will last as long but only time will tell.

If padding is important, then these gloves offer that and certainly cushion the lifter during many lifts. However, for me I can only give these gloves an average rating because of the cons and my concern that the stitching around the padding will come loose.
text_fidelity_b: Harbinger Flexfit Ultra WristWrap Lifting Gloves

text_fidelity_a:
FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player I bought this primarily to listen to Podcasts and some music while swimming laps. When it arrived, I was pleased with the hardware quality and ease of use. I loaded up some music and Podcasts and headed for the pool. It was relatively easy to clip the units to my goggles. The controls could be better, but are not terrible. I put it on, started playing a Podcast, put in my earplugs and started swimming. I had been concerned that my goggles might leak or come off during turns with these units clipped on, but it was not a problem at all.
The problem, though, was the sound. If sitting perfectly still underwater, it sounds decent. Pretty much on par with my 30-year-old one-speaker clock radio. However, even with earplugs, the noise of swimming and rushing water overpowers it. If I play familiar songs I can tell what I am listening to and somewhat enjoy them. However, forget about the spoken word. I had to turn the volume up really loud to be able to make out most of what was said on the Podcast due to distortion and background noise. And then it was just too loud to be enjoyable. In fact, I am sure that others in the pool could hear some sound from it. I tried to adjust it in every possible way, and followed the instructions precisely.
This seems like a good idea, but I am disappointed, especially for the cost.

Pros: Solid design, no earphones or earbuds, can still wear earplugs, easy to wear, stays on goggles and doesn't pull them off, easy to load songs.
Cons: Price, 1 GB of storage is a total insult, limited features and controls for an MP3 player, poor sound quality overshadows all else.
text_fidelity_b: FINIS Swimp3 1GB Waterproof MP3 Player

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin fēnix 5, Premium and Rugged Multisport GPS Smartwatch, Granite Blue Functionally speaking, this watch is pretty full featured. It has basic mapping and will accomodate most common activities very well. I like the build quality as well. I don't use any of the health monitoring features, so those are disabled to save battery life. Battery life is OK overall, not great. It loses about 8-10% on a one hour hike.

The reason for the one star review has to do with the non-replaceable battery, and the fact that this is a $500+ watch. I am on year two of owning this watch now and have seen about a 30% drop in battery life. That's pretty bad if you ask me. I predict I'll get another couple years out of it before the battery becomes unreliable for anything more than a run around the neighborhood. As such I can't recommend this watch at all as I think it is a very poor value... 3-5 years of use for a watch that costs upwards of $1000 for the high end models is totally unacceptable.
